correctness.rationale: For \(0<z<\sqrt{\alpha}\), the exact density ratio reduces to \(2((\alpha-1)\operatorname{artanh}(r)-\alpha r)\). For \(0<\alpha\le1\) this is strictly negative. For \(\alpha>1\), \(F(r)=\operatorname{artanh}(r)/r\) is strictly increasing from \(1\) to infinity, so there is exactly one root. Power-series comparison at \(r=1/\sqrt{\alpha}\) and \(r=\sqrt{3/\alpha}\) proves \(1<\kappa_\alpha<\sqrt{3}\), with the \(\alpha\le3\) upper range handled directly by support. Series matching in \(e=1/\alpha\) yields \(\kappa_\alpha^2=3-12/(5\alpha)+O(\alpha^{-2})\), hence the displayed expansion. No finite experiment is used to establish any infinite assertion.

value.rationale: The finding gives a complete, scale-free structural description of how Gamma skewness is distributed locally around the mean: the density is left-heavier through more than one standard deviation, then reverses exactly once, with a universal crossing below \(\sqrt{3}\). The boundary persists at \(\sqrt{3}\) standard deviations in the Gaussian limit while the imbalance amplitude vanishes. This directly refines the local geometry behind the motivating paper's central-variation comparison and is not an arbitrary finite slice or parameter substitution.
